fieldMappings.answer: Because the reliability of a data platform is a safety property when the platform feeds decisions about models, usage and revenue. I have spent years making small infrastructure trustworthy — hermetic builds, restore drills, telemetry that pages — and Anthropic is one of the few places where that same discipline is applied to systems with genuine consequences. I also want to work alongside people who treat interpretability and honesty about limitations as engineering requirements, not marketing. The Data Infrastructure charter, especially access control and financial pipeline integrity, is the version of that work I can do best.

Boundaries stated in the letter: no BigQuery/BigTable/Airflow/dbt/Spark operations, no petabyte-scale GCS/S3 replication or disaster recovery, no IAM/audit design at thousands-of-users scale. Strengths: PostgreSQL with migrations and rehearsed restores, backup automation, Linux and networking, hermetic Nix infrastructure-as-code, Go/Python tooling, telemetry and alerting.
